title: Role of financial information
blurb: Who uses it, when it is useful, NFRS characteristics and its limits.

topics.name: Who uses financial information?
topics.line: Primary users and other users, and what each needs.
topics.remember: Primary: investors and lenders. Others: employees, customers, suppliers, governments, public. Statements are for internal and external users.
topics.simple: Financial statements are read by many people. The investors and lenders are the main audience. Each group wants something different from the same numbers.
frames: chartup
Investors decide to buy, sell or hold shares and check risk and return.
bank
Lenders check whether loans and interest will be repaid.
people
Employees check the employer is stable and can pay and give retirement benefits.
building
Governments and regulators look at resource allocation, tax and national statistics.
gls: the main audience: investors and lenders
checking a business before a major acquisition

cards.mean: Buy, sell or hold equity shares. Assess risk and return, ability to pay dividends, and do due diligence before an acquisition
cards.ex: A shareholder decides whether to keep a holding.

cards.mean: Buy, sell or hold debt. Assess repayment of loans and interest, and creditworthiness before extending credit
cards.ex: A bank checks whether a loan will be repaid.

cards.mean: Employer's stability and profitability, and ability to pay remuneration and retirement benefits
cards.ex: Staff think about job security.

cards.mean: Whether the business will continue to exist, where they depend on the supplier long term
cards.ex: A buyer relying on a long-term supplier.

cards.mean: The likelihood of being paid when due
cards.ex: A supplier decides whether to give credit.

cards.mean: Resource allocation, regulation, taxation income and national statistics
cards.ex: A tax office checks tax income.

cards.mean: Trends in business prosperity, especially where it contributes to the local economy
cards.ex: A town that depends on one large employer.

items.q: Will loans and interest be repaid when due?
Should I buy, sell or hold the shares?
Will I be paid when due?
items.why: Suppliers and business partners assess the likelihood of payment.

items.q: Is the employer stable enough to pay my retirement benefits?
How much tax income can be expected?

topics.name: When is financial information useful?
topics.line: Decisions, stewardship, two assumptions and three statements.
topics.remember: Useful: informs decisions and shows stewardship. Assumptions: Accruals basis and Going concern, not prudence.
topics.simple: Financial information is useful if it helps people decide and shows how well managers used the resources entrusted to them.
frames: calendar
Accruals basis: record the effect of a transaction when it happens, not when cash moves.
hourglass
Going concern: assume the business continues for the foreseeable future.
building
The statement of financial position shows assets, liabilities and equity at a point in time.
chart
The statement of profit or loss shows income and expenses over a period.
gls: how well managers used the resources entrusted to them
recognise effects when they occur, not when cash is paid
the business is assumed to continue

cards.mean: Effects of transactions are recognised when they occur, not when cash is received or paid
cards.ex: A sale is recorded when made, even if paid later.

cards.mean: The business is assumed to continue in operation for the foreseeable future
cards.ex: Accounts are prepared as if the business carries on.

cards.mean: Financial position: assets, liabilities and equity at a point in time
cards.ex: A snapshot at year end.

cards.mean: Financial performance: income and expenses over a period
cards.ex: The year's income less its expenses.

cards.mean: Changes in financial position: how cash was generated and used in the period
cards.ex: Where the cash came from and went.

nodes.s: assets, liabilities, equity at a point in time
income and expenses over a period
how cash was generated and used

topics.name: Qualitative characteristics (NFRS)
topics.line: Two fundamental and four enhancing characteristics.
topics.remember: Fundamental: Relevance and Faithful representation. Enhancing: Understandability, Comparability, Verifiability, Timeliness.
topics.simple: The framework says useful financial information must have two core qualities. Four more qualities make it even more useful.
frames: target
Relevance: able to make a difference to a decision.
check
Faithful representation: complete, neutral and free from error.
scales
Comparability: like items treated alike over time and across businesses.
clock
Timeliness: in time to influence decisions.
gls: omitting or misstating it could influence user decisions
can be used to predict future outcomes

cards.mean: Capable of making a difference to user decisions. Predictive value, confirmatory value and materiality
cards.ex: Mina increased her shareholding after reading the statements.

cards.mean: Complete, neutral and free from error. Neutrality is supported by prudence
cards.ex: No bias in how information is chosen or shown.

cards.mean: Clear and concise. Relevant information must not be excluded merely because it is complex
cards.ex: Reasonable business knowledge is assumed.

cards.mean: Like transactions treated consistently over time and across businesses
cards.ex: A consistent depreciation policy over five years.

cards.mean: Different knowledgeable, independent observers could agree it is a faithful representation
cards.ex: Stating assumptions improves verifiability.

cards.mean: Available in time to influence decisions. Generally the older it is, the less useful
cards.ex: Some information stays useful for trend analysis.

nodes.s: makes a difference: predictive, confirmatory, material

topics.name: Cost constraint and limitations
topics.line: What limits the usefulness of financial reporting.
topics.remember: Cost constraint: benefits must justify cost. Limits: highly aggregated, backward-looking, omits non-financial data, historical cost, standardised format.
topics.simple: Financial statements are useful but not perfect. They cost money to make, and they have five weak points.
frames: table
Highly aggregated: many transactions are squeezed into a few figures.
calendar
Backward-looking: they cover a period that has already ended.
book
They omit non-financial data such as risks and governance.
money
Historical cost: values are not adjusted for inflation.
gls: many items combined into few figures
about the past, not the future
recorded at cost without adjusting for inflation

cards.mean: The benefits of information for all users should justify the cost of providing it
cards.ex: Do not produce a report that costs more than it helps.

cards.mean: Many transactions are condensed into a small number of figures, so individual components are hard to evaluate
cards.ex: One revenue figure hides many products.

cards.mean: Covers a period that has ended, while most users decide on future expectations
cards.ex: Identifies trends but cannot give all needed information.

cards.mean: No narrative on major operations, risks and opportunities, governance or management policies. These are in the strategic report
cards.ex: Risks are explained elsewhere.

cards.mean: Recorded at cost without accounting for inflation, so values become misleading, especially when inflation is high
cards.ex: An old asset shown at its old price.

cards.mean: Presentation is highly standardised while businesses are very diverse
cards.ex: One format may not fit every reader.

items.q: Many transactions condensed into a few figures
Covers a period that has already ended
No narrative about risks, governance or management policies
Assets recorded at cost despite high inflation
items.why: That is the historical cost basis.

items.q: One format for very different businesses

topics.name: Other sources of financial information
topics.line: Where users can find more than the financial statements.
topics.remember: Owner-managers: real-time management information. Banks: loan terms. Investors: negotiated. Suppliers: credit reports. Public: brochures and press.
topics.simple: Not everyone must rely on the published statements. Some users can get more information because of who they are.
frames: person
Owner-managers see budgets, forecasts and divisional accounts in real time.
bank
Banks may get extra access under loan agreements.
chartup
Potential investors may negotiate extra access for a major stake.
globe
The public can use brochures, press releases and media coverage.
gls: an agency that supplies credit standing reports
accounts for one part of the business
a large share that gives control

cards.mean: Internal management information on a real-time basis: budgets, forecasts, divisional accounts, future plans
cards.ex: The owner checks the forecast any day.

cards.mean: Often gain additional access under the terms of loan agreements
cards.ex: A loan contract requires extra reports.

cards.mean: May negotiate additional access when planning a major or controlling stake
cards.ex: Before buying a large share.

cards.mean: May obtain credit standing reports from agencies such as Experian
cards.ex: Checking a customer before giving credit.

cards.mean: Brochures, press releases, brokers' reports and media coverage
cards.ex: Reading a company announcement.

items.q: Budgets, forecasts and divisional accounts in real time
Extra access under the terms of a loan agreement
May negotiate extra access before taking a controlling stake
Credit standing reports from agencies such as Experian
